scenes.goal: buy what Venn found at the sales
scenes.opposition: Venn makes her wait while he threatens Margaret Lyle

turningPoint.description: Tom asks Nell to the harvest dance
turningPoint.evidence: "Would you come to it? With me, I mean."

evidence.goal: to see what he had bought at the sales
evidence.opposition: That Tuesday he made her wait because he was quarrelling.
evidence.outcome: "Ask me again on Friday," she said

scenes.goal: find out who poisoned Silas Venn
scenes.opposition: half the town had reason to, and the obvious suspect is the nephew

evidence.goal: "Who comes into his money?" Tom asked.
evidence.opposition: who knew the answer was half the town
evidence.outcome: Tom wrote Peter Venn's name in his notebook and underlined it twice.

scenes.goal: see for herself what Margaret Lyle is hiding
scenes.opposition: Margaret Lyle sends her away from the garden

turningPoint.description: Nell finds the foxglove border cut down and the bottle gone from the basket
turningPoint.evidence: Now every stem was cut down to the ground, and the cuttings were gone.

evidence.goal: At three she walked up to the vicarage with the vicar's library book
evidence.opposition: "Leave it on the hall table," she said.
evidence.outcome: one leaf for the heart, and two leaves for the grave

scenes.goal: bring Margaret Lyle to confess, and give Tom her answer
scenes.opposition: Margaret Lyle's composure, and Tom's doubts

turningPoint.description: Nell brings Tom to tea at the vicarage, where Margaret Lyle confesses
turningPoint.evidence: "Then come to tea at the vicarage," said Nell.

evidence.goal: Nell went to the police house on Thursday morning and told Tom Hale everything
evidence.opposition: She did not offer them sugar.
